messages:
Carla: Quick design question — I'm proposing we extend the capability manifest (v2) with explicit 'trust_level' and 'probe_policy' so adapters across hosted/dedicated/private can negotiate fallbacks without surprising ops. Example and rationale below.

Nikhil: +1 to explicit trust. We've hit a couple incidents where implicit assumptions meant telemetry disappeared silently. Need a minimum metrics contract too.

Priya: Would this require private adapters to open egress? Concerned about regulated customer installs. Can we make telemetry optional via a 'telemetry_bridge' opt-in?

Ben: My vote: define 'probe_policy' with values: passive, active, push. passive = runtime-only probes (no controlplane pings), active = controlplane can poll, push = adapter streams telemetry to controlplane. That lets security decide.

Carla: Draft manifest snippet (very small):
```json
{"capability_manifest_version":"2","trust_level":"isolated","probe_policy":"passive","telemetry_contract":["request_latency","failure_rate"],"optional":{"telemetry_bridge":"kinesis://arn:aws:..."}}
```

Priya: Suggest we standardize trust_level enums: public, tenant_isolated, hardware_isolated. Also add 'fallback_sequence' (array) to declare allowed fallthroughs, e.g. ["dedicated","hosted"] so runtime doesn't pick unexpected targets.

Nikhil: Also include a 'probe_retry_backoff' config so a mass rollout doesn't cause adapters to hammer the controlplane. We need bounds: max_retries and max_rps per tenant.

Ben: Ops note — many private installs strictly disallow outbound. We should support an 'offline' telemetry level where fallback decisions are local-only and controlplane dashboards show degradation. The manifest should express 'telemetry_annex.level' = none|summary|full.

Carla: Agreed. New proposal fields: trust_level, probe_policy, telemetry_annex (level, sampling_rate), fallback_sequence, probe_retry_backoff. Behavior: when telemetry_annex.level == none, controlplane must rely on synthetic probes/sampling and mark observability as degraded in UI.

Priya: Runtime implication: if trust_level == hardware_isolated we must forbid model_variant_fallbacks that require KV cache sharing or encrypted key exchange. Those operations should return a specific error code so SDKs can fallback gracefully.

Nikhil: Add 'manifest_signature' + version to detect drift between controlplane and adapter-provided manifest. Also include a soft-grace period for manifest mismatches to avoid rollouts triggering evictions.

Ben: TL;DR: Add trust_level + probe_policy + telemetry_annex + fallback_sequence + probe_retry_backoff; make telemetry optional; runtime enforces forbidden ops for high-isolation levels; ops gets a clear degraded UI signal.

Carla: I'll update the RFC with these fields and sketch a tiny state machine for fallback resolution (local -> fallback_sequence -> escalate to controlplane with reduced telemetry). Ping me if you want to review the RFC diff: @Priya @Nikhil. Thanks :raised_hands:
